reason: The cited evidence (E2) describes a much thicker (120 μm) Hf coating on the same alloy, showing reduced weight gain and a dense HfO2 layer, but does not support the specific 1–2 μm thickness, the PVD method, the claimed 70–80% reduction, or the mechanism of minimizing thermal expansion mismatch. E1 provides only general background on high-temperature alloys and does not support any specific premise.
premises: A thin (1–2 μm) Hf coating can be applied to a refractory HEA via PVD with strong adhesion.
The Hf coating will oxidize to form a continuous, adherent HfO2 scale at high temperature.
HfO2 scale acts as an effective oxygen barrier due to low oxygen diffusivity.
The HfO2 scale will reduce oxidation weight gain by 70–80% and maintain integrity at 1000 °C.
Careful control of coating thickness minimizes thermal expansion mismatch issues.
